newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ forex market closed for holiday.
newsitem.headline: NZ forex market closed for holiday.

text.p: New Zealand's foreign exchange market is closed on Monday for the Labour Day public holiday.
On Friday, the New Zealand dollar closed higher, ending locally at US$0.7037/44 and 67.23 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7005/10 and 66.90 at the open.
"It's finished the week quite well bid, given the big fall yesterday," said one currency trader.
On Thursday the Reserve Bank said monetary conditions were tighter than necessary, which prompted an immediate rally in the debt market and saw the Kiwi plummet a cent against the U.S. dollar.
But dealers said the currency had bounced strongly off 0.6980 with a change in sentiment.

"I think (there's) just a realisation that we're still a high-yielding currency. The global investor is still very yield sensitive and in that respect we're still going to see a lot of offshore demand for the Kiwi," the trader said.
"I think next week we may well have another crack at 71 (US) cents." -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
